title: Findings so far
html:
Findings so far

Last updated: 2026-11-12. Plain summaries; each links to its full result. Finding means it was the measure fixed in advance; lead means it was noticed afterwards or is from a small or exploratory run. Setup names are short labels for their OSO parameters: for example, the shared library is public at once, α 1, m 0.

Simulation

  • Finding: sharing at once is the big saving. To solve half the targets, traditional research needs 3.5× to 5.7× the money OSO needs, across five difficulties, mostly because work is repeated (no range computed on this ratio). Overview
  • Finding: flow-back makes agents choose to share. When agents decide whether to publish, they share 24% of their ideas at α 1 and 66% at α 0.2. With the rules deciding, α changes little. Overview
  • Lead: the knowledge reward matters once agents choose and money follows earnings (α 0.8: 1.8 of 2 targets with it, 0.4 without). Result

AI agents on Lean problems

  • Finding: lemmas help weaker models: with the lemmas a target needs, 3 of 5 models proved targets they never proved alone (DeepSeek: 4 of 16 tries alone, 12 of 16 with lemmas). Claude Opus and Sonnet proved everything alone. Panel

  • Finding, OSO against traditional (5 runs each): about the same in hard targets (OSO 2.0 of 4, traditional 1.6). Lead: traditional proved the same work twice about 20 times a run, OSO about 2. Race

  • Finding, Spend all, labs cannot stop (20 runs per setup): targets proved about the same (OSO α 0.2 against shared library +0.4, 95% range −0.1 to +0.9). Lead: the more value flowed back, the more lemmas labs proved (7.2 → 13.8 a run) and the more they built on each other. Results

  • Finding, May quit, labs may stop early (10 runs per setup): targets proved about the same (about 5 of 8 everywhere; OSO α 0.2 against shared library +0.0, range −0.8 to +0.8). Labs stopped after 5 to 8 rounds with half their money left. With flow-back they proved more lemmas (α 0.2: +2.2 a run, range +1.4 to +3.0). Results

  • Finding, Fair-prompt check (10 runs per setup, fair prompts, more money than Spend all): B5 much closer than in Spend all (OSO α 0.2: 4 of 10, shared library 3 of 10; difference +0.10, range −0.28 to +0.45), so the B5 question is open. Lemmas about doubled with flow-back (+8.7 a run, range +3.4 to +14.0). Labs' thinking often mentions flow-back pay; whether it drives their choices is not shown. Results

  • Finding, labs choose what to publish (M3, 10 runs per setup): AI labs published nearly every lemma at every α (99–100%; the simulation predicted 17% at α 1 and 93% at α 0.2). Their thinking shows why: the new-result reward is paid only on publishing, and they rarely weigh helping rivals. Lead: B5 proved in 8 of 10 runs at α 0.2, 4 of 10 at α 1. Results

  • Lead, harder targets (6 setups × 5 runs, 2026-11-09; too few runs for ranges): setups that publish at once proved 10.4 to 11 of 11 targets, traditional 7.6, but traditional ran at a higher price per token, so it had about a quarter less thinking; at the same price it reached 7 targets for $0.42, against $0.34 (shared library) and $0.48 (OSO α 0.2). The planner with a good strategy was cheapest, but without our hints it was among the worst. Flow-back alone (OSO α 0.2 against the shared library) gave no gain. Results

  • Lead, labs' saved thinking (148 runs): under flow-back, labs restate the rule and reason that a lemma earns when another lab uses it; in the shared library, that it earns nothing and may hand a rival the bounty. This shows they read the rule, not that it drives their choices. Flow-back so far

  • Finding, labs choose with the knowledge reward off (10 runs per α, 2026-11-10): flow-back did not clearly raise sharing. Share of lemmas published at once: 58% at α 1, 63% at α 0.8, 93% at α 0.2 (predicted 16, 16 and 93%). The planned difference, α 0.2 minus α 1, is +35 points with a range from −18 to +87: the direction predicted, but not shown. Labs proved few lemmas without the reward (8 at α 1). Results

  • Finding, labs choose on the bigger set (27 targets, 5 runs per setup, 2026-11-23): no clear difference. Lemmas published at once: 92% at α 1, 96% at α 0.2 (+4 points, range −3 to +12). Targets proved: traditional 20.0, α 1 20.6, α 0.2 21.2 of 27 (α 0.2 minus traditional +1.2, range −0.3 to +2.7). Lead: results built on another lab's work 6.4, 11.4 and 16.0 a run. Result

Correction (2026-11-08): every Lean run so far split flow-back by money spent instead of by graph weights (lines saved). Only 1–5% of earnings would have gone elsewhere and the counted measures are unaffected, but labs saw slightly wrong earnings. Details

Harness (2026-11-08): about 23% of model replies ran out of length and gave no answer, roughly 39% of the money spent, in every setup. A small test of high against medium effort showed no clear change. Details

Not yet tested: AI labs choosing when keeping is worth something (the new-result reward off), other models, and real mathematics designed by others. See the roadmap.
